messages:
maria (applied-ml): heads up — found a weird failure when bringing up qwen-72b-v2-8bit on the new runtime. evals show token misalignment after ~4k tokens. seems related to rotary+tokenizer offsets. logs below.

kevin (runtime): :eyes: can you paste the exact config you used? rotary params + tokenizer mapping sometimes mismatch between HF and internal vocab.

maria (applied-ml): sure. minimal repro: config override and load snippet:
```json
{"model_family":"qwen","rotary_embedding_base":10000,"rope_scaling":null,"vocab_size_override":65024}
```
Then we quantized with `bitsandbytes --4bit` profile and served with `--kv-cache=true`.

sara (research): did you try running the same checkpoint without quantization? if it still drifts maybe the tokenizer/vocab mapping is wrong.

maria (applied-ml): unquantized run looks fine. drift only appears after quant. quick diff from token stream around the error point:

```
expected_tokens: [..., 5023, 1601, 999, 2, 78, 901, ...]
observed_tokens: [..., 5023, 1601, 999, 2, 31589, 901, ...]
```

olga (eng): 31589 is out of range for the model vocab (should be <65024) but that value looks like a different tokenizer's id. Are we accidentally loading a Mistral/Gemma tokenizer somewhere?

maria (applied-ml): i grepped the bundle — the artifact contains two tokenizers: `tokenizer.json` (qwen) and `tokenizer.model` (legacy sentencepiece). runtime picks `tokenizer.model` when present.

kevin (runtime): ah that explains the mismatch. why only after quant?

maria (applied-ml): hypothesis: quantized weight loader uses a fast-path that bypasses some model metadata checks (to save startup time). as a result runtime didn't check tokenizer precedence and we served with the wrong vocab. non-quant path goes through full init and cleans up extra files.

infra-bot: deploy #1234 started for qwen-72b-v2-8bit on dev cluster (ci job 8892).

kevin (runtime): we should add a strict check: if multiple tokenizer artifacts exist, fail startup unless `tokenizer_precedence` set. quick patch idea:
```diff
+ if len(tokenizer_files) > 1 and not config.get('tokenizer_precedence'):
+     raise StartupError('multiple tokenizers found — set tokenizer_precedence')
```
I'll open a PR.

sara (research): also add a post-quantization hash check: confirm tokenizer.vocab_hash == model.metadata.vocab_hash. would catch corruption or cross-model mixes.

maria (applied-ml): for now i reran the quant pipeline with `--strip-legacy-tokenizer` and dev evals pass. attaching quick perf/quality snapshot (unquant vs quant-stripped vs quant-with-legacy):

```
BLEU-like eval on prompt-set (1000 prompts):
- unquantized: 0.872
- quant-stripped: 0.861
- quant-with-legacy: 0.402  <-- catastrophic
Tokens until drift (median):
- unquantized: >32k
- quant-stripped: >32k
- quant-with-legacy: ~4.2k
Latency p95 (single request):
- unquantized: 420ms
- quant-stripped: 190ms
- quant-with-legacy: 180ms
```

olga (eng): good catch. add a test in onboarding CI that runs a short token-consistency check after quant artifact generation. simple script: feed a deterministic prompt, compare tokenized ids to HF tokenizer dump.

kevin (runtime): agreed. i'll add the tokenizer precedence check + metadata assert in runtime and mark it hotfix for dedicated. patch link: https://git.redwood/infer/PR/3691 (WIP).

maria (applied-ml): one more oddity — some Mistral derivs use rotary_base=4096, Qwen uses different scaling. when we force a model to use runtime default rotary_base we see small quality deltas on longer contexts. we should store rotary params in model metadata and honor them during compilation/quantization.

sara (research): yea, parameters to capture: rotary_base, rope_scaling, use_alibi(boolean), vocab_size. add to modelcard.

olga (eng): will update the model-asset spec. PR to spec repo after lunch.

deploy-bot: rollout blocked: runtime hotfix required for tokenizer precedence.

maria (applied-ml): ok thanks everyone. i'll re-run onboarding with the strip flag for prod candidates and follow up once runtime PR merges.

kevin (runtime): will ping when PR is ready for review. thanks for the clear repro, maria. :tada:
